Review: Took a drive to the quaint village of Siniawan to have a drink at the Bikalan. The Bikalan is a pub and restaurant owned by a very friendly couple, Andy and Grace. The pub itself has a lovely atmosphere, it is by the river, in a rustic cowboy like setting. They had Guinness and Tiger on tap. We tried the local food and it was absolutely delicious! Author: Steven Quint
Review: I lived near the Siniawan area for 5 years as one of the few Western residents. The opening of the Bikalan was most welcome. A lot of restaurants in the area tend to copycat one another in terms of how their food tastes and how you get …MoreI lived near the Siniawan area for 5 years as one of the few Western residents. The opening of the Bikalan was most welcome. A lot of restaurants in the area tend to copycat one another in terms of how their food tastes and how you get served. Well, the Bikalan is definitely original. Their food isn't merely great, it stands out. I am friends with the owners Grace and Andy, after visiting the Bikalan numerous times, and they're super friendly and conversational. They run their restaurant with a positive energy that goes unmatched. Meet them and see for yourself. The live bands and customer service are some of the best I've ever encountered. You won't find this anywhere else in the area. With all this great stuff you'd think it would be expensive, but it's actually a really great deal. I've entertained parties of 10+ people at the Bikalan without straining my wallet. You'll get more in return than what you pay.
Location: 33 Pekan Siniawan, Siniawan, Bau, Sarawak

Author: Rider Chris
Review: As I've travelled quite extensively in South East Asia, I must say Bikalan is one of my favourite bars that I've been to. Situated just about 25KM from Kuching city, Bikalan is a laid back bar, serving authentic local cuisine and they offer …MoreAs I've travelled quite extensively in South East Asia, I must say Bikalan is one of my favourite bars that I've been to. Situated just about 25KM from Kuching city, Bikalan is a laid back bar, serving authentic local cuisine and they offer a great range of alcohol/foods to fill up your night. Their food/drinks pricings are quite affordable and we really enjoyed the Bikalan, you don't get this kind of atmosphere anywhere in Malaysia. Imagine having a good draught beer next to a river in a Belian wood shop house in Siniawan's historic main bazaar.The owners (Andy & Grace) are down to the earth person. If you're going there, ask Andy about the history of the place, he would love to explain it to you. Tips: If you're going here, make sure you arrange cab/taxi/grab on your way back in advance. Alternatively, you can stay at the Tian Xia homestay at the night market area. (Just Google it)

Review: This is hands down the worst meal I've ever had. Shockingly bad. We left wondering if the chef (or anyone else working there for that matter) had ever eaten food before. The ambiance is nice, but the place smells of lemon-scented moth balls. The chef's noodles are just fried noodles in tasteless, gelatinous glop. The mango duck might've been good, but the duck was served as some kind of mayonnaise salad. The broccoli and mushrooms were half hot, half cold, all bland. The thai chicken was the driest chicken I've had. It is served with a bafflingly bitter salad that does not compliment the dish at all. One star because the house wine was fine. Literally everything else we've eaten in Kuching has been amazing--so why is this place so bafflingly bad? Do yourself a favor and eat anywhere else.

Author: syaiful akmar
Review: Now, I owe this review for about 4 months. I went to this place at the Green Hill. Location exactly behind Harbour View hotel. The environment is good, restaurant looks really clean and neat. Walk inside the restaurant and immediately I …MoreNow, I owe this review for about 4 months. I went to this place at the Green Hill. Location exactly behind Harbour View hotel. The environment is good, restaurant looks really clean and neat. Walk inside the restaurant and immediately I felt hot and humid atmosphere. So I chose to sit at the table outside at the entrance. Immediately the waiter came and gave me the menu. I know what to order. One Nan Cheese and one Chicken Biryani. Waited for about 2 minutes until my drink arrived. That was fast. About 10 minutes i got my Biryani. Earlier the waiter did mention for Nan Cheese i have to wait for 15 minutes. I don't mind at all and it did came as told. The Biryani is fabulous with very soft, juicy chicken curry. The curry is not that spicy and have a unique flavour compared to other Indian restaurant in Kuching. But put that aside, lets talk about the Nan Cheese. First the nan is soft, not the average rubbery kind that you ever ate. The cheese filler inside the nan is a lot. I mean a lot. I would say the Nan Cheese in Ceylonese is the best in Sarawak. I could safely say it because I travelled a lot and ate a lot of it if they are available in the restaurants. Author: Iise Chew
Review: Balkanico Pizza is, to me, hands down, the most authentic hand-made pizza in Kuching. …MoreBalkanico Pizza is, to me, hands down, the most authentic hand-made pizza in Kuching.Our pizzaiolo (fancy word for pizza-maker hehe) who goes by the name of Aleksander hails all the way from Montenegro, Southeast Europe.I love how Aleksander makes the dough from scratch, kneading the dough with strength - it comes out from the oven as a perfect thin crunchy crust.Fresh from the oven, the pizza is amazing- from the texture, to the cheese used, and the freshness of the ingredients, it's a culinary heaven for the tongue.The greatest highlight to me is the home-made pesto sauce - this blended green basil mixture complements the pizza perfectly! This pesto has such a strong garlicky taste, it simply made the pizza stand out immediately. He makes the pesto with freshest ingredients daily.If you are a lover of garlic and strong spices, you can't miss this pizza with its pesto. It's too good. In my life, I've never had pizza with a stronger garlic tang. For those who aren't really fans of garlic however, you could always request for lesser or no pesto at all.Located behind the Fairland Hidden Bar, this rustic looking area makes for a most picturesque spot.If you are in Kuching, this is definitely a must try.

Location: Wayang St, Kuching, Sarawak

You are welcomed with smiles and friendly service. Ordered the mi kolok, laksa sarawak and …MoreI have to give this place 5 star for it's great service & hospitality, good foods quality & taste &  clean yet rustic-chic kind of feel restaurant. Author: Dorene
Review: It is a small cozy cafe with friendly staff. There is a variety of dishes at reasonable prices in their menu. We had the Sarawak Laksa and Grilled Chicken Rice with additional order of Stir-fried Mixed Vegetables. …MoreIt is a small cozy cafe with friendly staff. There is a variety of dishes at reasonable prices in their menu. We had the Sarawak Laksa and Grilled Chicken Rice with additional order of Stir-fried Mixed Vegetables.In my opinion, the Sarawak Laksa was quite similar to Penang Curry Mee with a mixed of 'beehoon & yellow noodles' but it had lesser coconut milk and less spicy too. But, the curry flavour was awesome with added fresh lime juice! It also came with prawns and a generous portion of beansprouts and lean chicken pieces.The grilled chicken was tender and juicy. The rice was also fluffy and soft. The stir-fried mixed vegetables was not overcooked but the gravy was too thick and sweet. Perhaps, it was due to huge doses of oyster sauce in it.In a nutshell, it is a nice restaurant and their Sarawak Laksa is worth trying.

Don't be shy, the place is frequented by mostly locals and they're friendly, ask nicely if …MorePaying homage to the late Anthony Bourdain by enjoying his #1 favorite food in the world - Sarawak Laksa. The place is packed and seats are limited. Don't be shy, the place is frequented by mostly locals and they're friendly, ask nicely if you could sit with them to save some time instead of waiting for an empty table. I definitely recommend trying the Sarawak Laksa, you have 3 noodles choices - bee hoon, yellow mee or both. The broth is smooth, not too spicy but the chicken and prawns ❤. Love! Overall, amazing food and very friendly staff. Parking is limited so I would recommend you just Grab here. It's in the heart of China Town so finding transportation is easy.

Maybe I'm biased that it has been highly praised by the late Anthony Bourdain, but I do find the broth to be flavourful, the succulent chicken comes in sliced chunks rather than (too small) shredded pieces, and the sambal is excellent!Simple old style cafe ambiance coupled with quick and friendly staff. There are other good dishes to try out: popiah, porridge, kaya toast, half boiled eggs etc. All pretty good and worth a go.There is no allocated parking bays and you'll be literally parking along the side of the road. Due to its popularity, it can be difficult to find a space. And sadly, this is not wheelchair friendly.Tips: if ordering laksa, ask for more sambal (it's usually not enough) and if ordering popiah, you can customise what goes into it.

Review: Went to this motorsport themed restaurant for the first time. I really enjoy the decor and the ambient inside the restaurant, as I'm motorsport enthusiast myself. The menu and cutlery already set on the table and after 5minutes the waitress …MoreWent to this motorsport themed restaurant for the first time. I really enjoy the decor and the ambient inside the restaurant, as I'm motorsport enthusiast myself. The menu and cutlery already set on the table and after 5minutes the waitress came to take our orders. We tried both western and local cuisine and they absolutely nailed it for me. The fish and chips was crispy yet soft inside, the fries and garnish was well seasoned, the dip sauce was different from any other places, although I do wish they give us more of that sauce, the fried keau tiaw was well seasoned, plenty of prawns, squid, and chickens with it. Here's the little things I like about the food; they didn't overcook anything, they properly cooked the squid, they properly cleaned the prawns, that showed me a quality chef/kitchen crew in the kitchen. As I were sharing the food with my partner, the waitress came and gave us an empty plate for our convenient without us asking for it, now that's a + in customer service. I got nothing to say for the decor except that I really love it and I feel at home with it. The only downside for me is the pricing is kinda at the medium to high area, although they due compensate it with portions that can fulfill 2 people. In the end, with the theme of the restaurant, the quality of the food, the subtle things the waiter/waitress did, it was money well spent and definitely a good place to choose. I definitely have found a place to hangout or have dinner.
Location: Lot 244, Ground Floor, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, Kuching, Sarawak

Review: Muffin is fresh, light and fluffy. All the ingredients were hot so the cheese melts and sticks to the bread for oozy bites! At RM5, I'll have this over McMuf***s any time. …MoreMuffin is fresh, light and fluffy. All the ingredients were hot so the cheese melts and sticks to the bread for oozy bites! At RM5, I'll have this over McMuf***s any time.Bagel was similarly fresh - crispy on the outside and soft inside. Considerably less dense than others I've had overseas but still good. Excellent value for money - RM18 for a layer of smoked salmon & cream cheese plus a good helping of salad and scrambled eggs on the side. The eggs were a little too salty for my tastes, but they had textbook "scrambled" texture which is actually hard to achieve.Scone was a bit small (each serving is 1 scone). It came with jam and cream cheese while we're more used to jam and fresh cream which helps to balance the heaviness of scones.Meatball noodles were ok, but there's a heavy hand with seasoning.Choc milkshake was more like iceblended milo, but kid was happy with it so no complains.Restaurant tries to be family friendly with high chairs and kiddy utensils available for use, but space is cramped and seating is on stools so there are still challenges with bags and umbrellas and older kids who need to kneel on chairs.The wait was ok (we arrived around 10 and it wasn't too busy), but the second order we made after the first items started arriving took till we finished everything before it showed up.All in, an excellent breakfast where east and west met and had a ball of a time! The breads transported us to a posh cafe, but the ambience and "damage" to the wallet were firmly in the arena of the coffee shop 'round the corner.

Author: Swee Kee Chew
Review: One of the earliest foodcourt in town; before when the word was in vogue. Leased by the temple across the road by proxy of the Teochew Association.This foodcourt serves as a theater to the temple opposite it. It's open …MoreOne of the earliest foodcourt in town; before when the word was in vogue. Leased by the temple across the road by proxy of the Teochew Association.This foodcourt serves as a theater to the temple opposite it. It's open throughout the year except when the space is used by the temple for its worship & diety's birthday. It operates almost 24 hours by its various vendors at different times.The Teochew Bak Muay (porridge) starts around midnight with its prep work, and starts selling around 1am. until everything is sold, which is around 9 am.The drinks stall begins around 6 am. with 2 rotation of personnels, and ends around 9:30 pm.The Bak-E'nee/Pork Satay (meatball & Yong Tauhu) stall picks up where the Bak Muay ends - from around 10 am. to around 4 pm. This stall closes on Friday following its long-observed tradition of Christians abstaining from meat on that day.The Kolo Mee by the 3 sisters starts at 6 to around 4 pm. or when it's sold out.The Kueh Chap (mixed offals) stall starts from 7 am to around 11 am., and again from around 5 pm. until late evening. Also different personnel from the same family. Porridge is served with braised duck in the evening.The Laksa stall is a new unknown entity despite its banner advertising it to the contrary. Long before there was a lone stall in front of the Bak Muay selling Laksa, which was only so-so; he has long retired.Lastly, there's a Zhi-Char stall near the stage that only operates in the evening, with sharp cleaver, who's made a killing during the go-go days of the 80s. If you don't patronize his stall, you'd better not sit at his table.
Restaurant: Lau Ya Keng Foodcourt 阳春台茶室

Review: (Translated by Google) In addition to a lot of meat or meat dishes in Kuching, there are also vegetarian dishes. In addition, in recent years, there are more and more vegetarians. They are vegetarian and healthy, and love the earth🌍.Come on, today Fat Niu will introduce a vegetarian dish, otherwise I always feel like I am a carnivore.Fig free cafe <Humble House>Usually fried rice will be mixed with packaged vegetables, eggs, seafood or meat and other ingredients.But because it is a vegetarian dish, it usually replaces seafood or meat with vegetables.And besides the grains of fried rice, it’s not the kind of lumps (I don’t like to eat lumps of lumps), I also eat fresh vegetables!!!There is no vegetarian food (maybe too fragrant to eat quickly, I didn’t see it, but I am not used to eating vegetarian food because it feels like a weird taste when refrigerated. If there are friends who are not used to it, I highly recommend ordering like me That's right!!!🤩🤩🤩)In addition, I was very surprised to eat the dried bean curd that will snap QQ. It is a fresh one. If you don't chew it carefully, it is really hard to find that it is small square particles. In addition, the olives in it are the flesh of olives, which are salted and made into olive horns or drums. I ate olive horns in it. The salty and salty flavor will make the whole taste better. Although TA has a strong pepper flavor, it still tastes salty. Generally speaking, it is not greasy (the photo can be seen). It is really hard to fry and not lazy to eat the distinct grains of rice. There are also service staff who are very considerate and ask if you want to eat eggs, because the vegetarians do not add eggs, but vegetarian food is fine.The honey lemon is also very special. It also contains ginger but you can drink honey and lemon flavor.And the environment is very comfortable, they will put on mosquito coils at night.Fig free cafe <Humble House>Operation hours: 10am-8:30pm (monday off)Rating: 7/10Price: Fried rice with olives(olive dabai fried rice): RM 7.80Hot honey lemon: RM 3.80The menus here are all in English because they are related to tourist attractions, but don’t worry that the service staff will introduce them to you in Chinese.So in addition to vegetarians, Muslim friends can also come and enjoy it.Next time I will put the environment here and how to get there in my youtube ✌(Original)古晋除了非常多的肉或荤料理，还是有素食料理。加上近几年素食者也开始越来越多，吃素健康又爱地球🌍。来，今天胖妞就介绍一样素料理不然老感觉我是肉食动物。Fig free cafe <寒舍>通常炒饭里会加包装的蔬菜、鸡蛋、海鲜或肉类等其他食材混合。但因为是素食料理，通常会是以素料代替海鲜或肉类。而这里除了饭炒的粒粒分明不是那种一坨一坨的(超不喜欢吃绵绵一坨坨的)，我还吃到新鲜的蔬菜!!!没有素料(可能太香吃快了，没看到，但我本身就不习惯吃素料因为感觉就是冷藏制作会怪怪的味道，如果有朋友和我一样不习惯的，非常建议和我一样点这就对了!!!🤩🤩🤩)此外我还很惊讶😲的吃到会弹牙QQ的豆干，是新鲜那种，如果没认真咀嚼，真的很难发现，是四方小颗粒的。另外里头有橄榄就是橄榄的果肉，是以盐腌制而制作成榄角或榄鼓。在里头我吃的了橄榄角，有咸香咸香的味道也会让整个口感更好。虽然TA的胡椒味很浓但还是吃的到那咸香味。 整体来说不会油腻(照片可见)真的很用力的炒没偷懒，才能吃上那粒粒分明的米粒。还有服务人员非常的贴心会问吃不吃蛋因为吃斋的是不加蛋的但吃素可以。还有蜂蜜柠檬也很特别还放了姜但又可以喝到蜂蜜和柠檬味。而且环境很舒适，晚上他们还会点上蚊香。Fig free cafe <寒舍>Operation hours: 10am - 8:30pm (monday off)Rating : 7/10价格: 橄榄炒饭(olive dabai fried rice) : RM 7.80热蜂蜜柠檬(honey lemon): RM 3.80这里都是英文菜单因为是旅游景点的关系但不要担心服务人员们都会用中文和你介绍哦。所以这里除了素食者其实穆斯林朋友也可以来享用。下次会在我的youtube里放上这里的环境和怎么到那里哦✌

Choose 2 desserts: creme brulee and panna cotta. The creme brulee's sugar coating was too hard and too burnt in some places. I am not too familiar with panna cotta; usually served with a coulis. it was a nice experience although a bit monotone taste. We spend somewhat over RM 100 for 2.If you have a birthday to celebrate you can have your table specially decorated. A nice idea.Ambiance and staff are top 5 stars. I think there was enoki mushrooms used, but just the right amount so that the taste of enoki was not too overpowering. Could not quite get a taste of any other mushrooms (if there were) & spinach was sparingly used. Wish there were more ingredients! My friend had a medium rare rib eye, & she kept saying how she loved the charred outer, burnt bits of steak, but juicy & tender within. She enjoyed the sauce accompanying the steak thoroughly! And as she was given a pesto in olive oil too, I dipped the crust of my pizza in the oil, was so satisfying! Her veggies were really crunchy & retained their colours well. The chef(s) here is/ are obviously very skilful!Ambience is alright, could be improved if the hanging creepers & fake flowers felt outdated & might be better removed (felt like I was at a Malay wedding instead of a restaurant), so that the bare beauty of the wooden interiors could be better appreciated. Lights were too glaring & intrusive. The narrow staircase leading to the dining area upstairs was difficult for my friend who had weak knees, so she wished there was an elevator! Author: Paul Ooi
Review: At Jalan Pudungan and right on the rooftop of UTC Building is where this Topspot Foodcourt is located. We stayed at the Imperial Riverbank hotel which is minutes walk to this destination. We stayed at the Imperial Riverbank hotel which is minutes walk to this destination. Mind you, if you have knee problem I advise you to look for the entrance with a service lift to take you up to the food court. It is indeed a steep stairs climb up, not easy & not advisable for elderly people.... so keep that in mind.Once you are at the top of this foodcourt, walah !! you will see many stalls lighted up with colourful neon lights bearing their stall’s name. Fresh seafoods on display and live stock in water tank for the picking. Mainly seafoods stall, halal as well. Then they have satay stalls too. According to the review we read, #25 is a safe choice to pick for a satisfying seafood dinner experience. We were pleasantly served by friendly staff and the seafood we had were as expected, we really had a great time and value for money. Prices here are reasonable except for drinks, I ordered the “am bela” fruit drinks that cost RM5.00 a glass which I felt expensive as it is a local fruit drink. Anyway, moving on to the taste of the seafood and the freshness, they were really delicious to taste & fresh especially the steamed fish in spicy lime sauce, was truly awesome ( please see photo ). The Kuching Öh Chian”  is very much different from the Penang ones, it is like eating crispy biscuit with oyster in it for the picking and they are really indeed tasty.The seating were mostly in the open air style with some partial shelter, pretty dimly lighted which I find not to my liking.  Crowded at night at time just like “pasar” atmosphere, noisy and full of people having a good time, chatting and eating at the same time. Overall, it is a place full of energy with busy activity, which is a good thing. Do go there....It is a highly recommended place to come for fresh seafood, forget the long drive to the sea side in Kampung Buntal seafood restaurant. We tried the Lim Hock Ann Seafood restaurant ( please read my review of the restaurant ) and were disappointed.

One positive point is they are hardworking enough to clarify and check. Author: Mochin H
Review: I'd have given this place more stars if the service hadn't been a disappointment. 1st off, let me tell of a previous experience in this same restaurant wherein we had already ordered a certain dessert along with our mains, after we were …MoreI'd have given this place more stars if the service hadn't been a disappointment. 1st off, let me tell of a previous experience in this same restaurant wherein we had already ordered a certain dessert along with our mains, after we were done with our mains we requested for the dessert to come but learned they had ran out of it & had neither bothered to reserve 1 for us when we had ordered it earlier nor inform us that the dessert is no more. Through that experience, this time we thought we were smart to ask our waitress the items that are unavailable. Interestingly, she told us there are no prawns, petai & oysters. Imagine our shock because prawn is a very important ingredient in Thai foods. And so, being fans of Pad thai (a stir-fried rice noodle dish similar to our local kueh tiaw) we further inquire what ingredient would instead be replaced with the prawn in the Pad thai. At this point, we are aware of the lack of English skill of our waitress who probably also has -1 intellect. After we repeated our question many times in Malay, she finally conceded to request the help of her colleague whom although doesn't necessarily posses perfect English but at least she understood us. Through her, we received the 2nd shock to our already waning interest in the place (we were already considering leaving, you see), she told us that they do have prawns & only thing unavailable is petai! What?!!! So...what was all that about with the previous waitress?! Turns out, only a specific dish with petai is unavailable which also has prawns & oysters in it so she with the low intellect unwittingly told us that all these ingredients are unavailable...Ah...what a way to ruin my mother's birthday dinner. The manager should also be reprimanded for hiring such a lousy staff especially in a location where westerners are known to frequent. In conclusion, the food was good but that staff has got to go.

Review: Keeper's Ground, a café located in The Spring Mall, serves perhaps the finest gourmet dishes one can find in Kuching. …MoreKeeper's Ground, a café located in The Spring Mall, serves perhaps the finest gourmet dishes one can find in Kuching.Certainly on the pricier side, here is where I mouth the clichéd saying, 'you pay for what you get'.Speaking of the environment of this place, the designs are beautiful - a very sleek & modern feel with lush greens bringing a certain freshness to the place. The service is excellent - the team is ever ready to serve guests.Keeper's Ground has their very own bakery, where their pastries are served fresh from the oven. I particularly love their cinnamon roll - crisp at the outside, fluffy in the inside with a sinful sugar coating and a rich cinnamon punch. Their cakes are spectacular, and very artfully displayed for the perusal of customers.Their cuisine served is top-notch. Dishes like the 'Multigrain Fried Rice' is Michelle's favourite - consistent every single time we visit this café, the rich colours of the red rice, purple cabbage, coupled with quinoa never fail to impress. None of the dishes I've tried here as ever failed me. The KGB Burger (is that ?Keeper's Gourmet Burger?) serves a succulent home-made beef patty with crunchy sweet potato fries.Keeper's Ground has a rich selection of teas and beverages. I've tried some of their flower teas (Rose of my life, lavenders in provence) and they were really nice.Aside from the pricey part, I easily give this place a 5-star. It is true, in this case, that you pay for you get.

That sets it a class apart …MoreThe food here is of a standard that if it came in a blind bag, you could have told me it came from some good grade restaurant in another metropolitan city like Singapore or even New York and I'd have believed you. That sets it a class apart from nearly all the restaurants I've patronized in all my visits to Kuching.Sweet potato fries were soft inside, crispy outside and came with a dipping sauce that elevated the experience.Burgers were very interesting - there's a crispy Korean chicken version and another w Japanese soft shell crab. Buns are well crusted but soft and airy on the inside.Chicken bolognese was very enjoyable - no stringy meat pieces to chew through yet still satisfyingly meaty.My large party with many children left the table with all plates emptied so that's testament to how good the food here is.I heard this was a new location for the restaurant - from the full house crowd at lunch during a work day in a new development, I'd say they have maintained their high standards and have drawn a very loyal following.We'll done!
Location: Lot 49, Block D1, Saradise, Kuching, Sarawak

Review: Pretty good western food, but ambience a little lacking. We arrived on Thursday night for dinner. Ken's kitchen was already pretty full. The decor is clean and modern, with an open kitchen. The downside is that with many customers, the …MorePretty good western food, but ambience a little lacking. We arrived on Thursday night for dinner. Ken's kitchen was already pretty full. The downside is that with many customers, the noise levels are high and it reflects off the various surfaces - so this is not a cosy, quiet, restaurant. Review: I liked the ambience of this place. The staff were absurdly welcoming and friendly. It's situated next to the river and the busy waterfront where the night comes alive. …MoreI liked the ambience of this place. The staff were absurdly welcoming and friendly. It's situated next to the river and the busy waterfront where the night comes alive.The restaurant was originally built as a watch post for the local detention centre circa 1879.The interior has been renovated, but not extremely. Some visitors may complain it needs a redecoration. I say it's like giving plastic surgery to an aging supermodel. Sometimes the old is charming and beautiful. If you look up, the wooden beams look original. It's a nice touch missing in the modern era.Now for the food. I only had one dish, and I'll update when I have another. I had mushroom soup. It didn't come from a can, and real mushrooms and cream were involved. Real food can never ever dip below a 8/10 for me because of the rarity of it. I liked it. It wasn't haute cuisine but it was something that a good friend would make for you on a nice evening together.I'll be back tomorrow night.

They have variety types of fish, prawn and squid. Other than seafood, there is also vegetables and chicken. Soup is also available in this restaurant.For dinner, I have tried crab soup with corns. They really use crab meat, not the instant crab. And its tasty. I order the soup for small serving as there is only 2 person eating(me and my friend). However the portion is big as me and my friend get to eat around 3 small bowls each for only RM8. The price for drinks is very cheap. Its the same as cafeteria price such as ice lemon tea for only less than RM2. We also tried blackpepper chicken and it is very delicious and juicy. It tasted like a grill chicken. And also the price is just RM8 for 2 person eating. So it is very affordable as you can share with your friend RM4 each. For vegetable, we choose cangkuk manis cook with egg. And also for RM8 per serving. For rice, it is only cost RM1.30 for a bowl. I recommend this restaurant as it really worth, the serving is very fast and the staff is friendly and helpful.For lunch, they have set menu for example butterchicken with salted egg rice. This place often full especially during dinner. However u can always make early booking as they have extra place to eat upstairs. For booking purpose, you can always google Bukit Mata Seafood Restaurant and there is their contact number.

Review: Pardon me for getting lyrical about the porkribs and the french fries!  A simple dish, but one served as it should be!  The pork ribs are not so meaty as one gets at other places, but this is how pork ribs are eaten in the West.  By the …MorePardon me for getting lyrical about the porkribs and the french fries!  A simple dish, but one served as it should be!  The pork ribs are not so meaty as one gets at other places, but this is how pork ribs are eaten in the West.  By the way, I eat them with my fingers.  So asked the waiter for a little bowl with water to clean my fingers and that came promptly! As to personal taste, the BBQ sauces (I took the original, my partner the smoky) were a bit too sweet.  But still enjoyable.  And then the french fries. Like they are eaten in Belgium (the birth country of the 'french' fries!).  Decent size (not the skinny ones from the international chains), fried to perfection:  crispy outside, fluffy inside!  One would think they were made from scratch and fried twice!  Best french fries eaten in Kuching sofar. Asked for some mayonnaise for my fries and that also came promptly. And not the sweet salad dressing, but real mayo!  Yummy!.  To top it all off, shared a huge banana split ice cream.  Lovely icecream!  Portions are big at Howdys!  Enjoyed the meal.  Definitely recommended if you want to taste real porkribs and real 'french' fries!

Author: Merr Peng
Review: We were looking for a place for New Year’s Eve dinner and found Howdy on Google. It had good ratings so we decided to give it a shot. Boy, was dinner a regular mess. …MoreWe were looking for a place for New Year’s Eve dinner and found Howdy on Google. It had good ratings so we decided to give it a shot. Boy, was dinner a regular mess.We made a reservation for 8PM. All food was PRE-ORDERED. Note that our orders were neatly written down on an Excel spreadsheet and hand-delivered to the restaurant. At around 7:45PM, one server (possibly the head waitress) asked if they could start serving the food but we preferred to wait for our last party members, who came 5 minutes before 8. We sat down and someone took our drink orders. Everything went smoothly until about that point.Let me start with their disorganization. Servers running around all over the place, bumping into each other and haphazardly serving dishes and drinks. There is a great system in grillhouses like this in the United States - ONE server is assigned to a certain area, so he/she waits on specific tables at a given time. At Howdy, we seemed to have all sorts of different people coming by and each time we had an issue, they all appeared lost and uncertain.Disappearing Drinks.Like I said, service was haphazard. Our drinks came randomly and intermittently. Not only did they miss out on multiple people's drinks, they added drinks to the bill that we didn't order. We had to ask a couple of times for the missing drinks and slowly, one by one, they came. Except an iced milk tea. I guess iced milk tea is hard to catch in the wild. We waited and asked and waited and asked, multiple servers, at least four or five separate times throughout dinner. The last person we asked, we could even hear him shouting to the kitchen for an iced milk tea. But guess what? Iced milk tea is a very evasive creature. It never came.The Case of the Forgotten Steak.Food. I understand, this isn't the United States (as per my reference to restaurants in the US). So I came in not expecting too much from their food. I'm fair - as long as the food was reasonably tasty, I'd write a good review. Even then, I was disappointed. Howdy is supposed to specialize in ribs. Baby back ribs, well-cooked, will come off the bone easily. Their baby back ribs did not. They were much drier and tougher than what we expected. The lamb shank was the same. Dry, tough, hard to cut. Tried someone's salmon - it was also dry and a little rubbery. Mashed potatoes were dry and not very mashed. Well done steaks were not well done… at all. The second steak we ordered was a JOKE. After everyone had received their dishes, we realized one person did not have theirs. So we asked, and the server left and never came back. So we asked again, and the server left and never came back. Finally, we asked a guy who looked like he could be a manager or head waiter. He left and came back with a newly printed bill. That's when we realized they had never made the order. The steak came at 8:58PM, 2 minutes short of an hour of waiting. And yes, like I said, it was not well done as requested. We sent it back to have it fixed. At the end of the night, they charged us full price for the forgotten steak.The one upside I can think of is the servers were polite. As disorganized as the system was, they were polite and they did (try to) cater to the issues that arose during dinner (emphasis on “try”). Everything else was disappointing. Howdy certainly seemed like a decent place to go. Perhaps they work better with smaller parties and perhaps it is decent on any other day of the year, hence the high ratings. But tonight it certainly didn't live up to the 4+ stars. I won't come again nor will I bring anyone I know. Not recommended.
Location: Brighton Square, Sublot 8, Block 16 Ground, Jalan Song, Kuching, Sarawak

Roast piglet came with meat uncut so had to ask them, several times also, to cut it up so we can eat. Author: Lenny “Red Monster” NJS
Review: We booked a room with 16 adults and kids for Dad’s Birthday. We choose the menu and everything was discussed before the day, long before the day for the dinner. …MoreWe booked a room with 16 adults and kids for Dad’s Birthday. We choose the menu and everything was discussed before the day, long before the day for the dinner.We arrived and was led to our room where table was set and seems like it’s good to go, I went to told the captain they could start serve our dinner. Went back to the room and wanna pour myself some tea, found my glass was fill with finger print and water mark, went ahead and check all the glass and table ware, plate is chipped, glass is dirty, bowl is stained. Not Impressed, Not at all.Next was even bizarre, they served all our 8 course dinner within 20 mins!! I booked a room and get menu sort out so I could get a banquet experience where dishes by dishes will be serve accordingly, not rush out in 1 lum sum!! As you could imagine, everything was right in the middle of the table and everyone is rushing to eat everything instead of sitting down and relax, Undisturbed in our room.Went and talked to the captain or manager when asking for bill, she act blur and said “ you should had told us in that way “, seriously? 8 course in 25 mins?Turn out they have a wedding reception going on so they try to rush out order out before they proceed to serve theirs! What a joke.Guess what, I always told everyone I knew or come in town in regards how reputable Lok Tien is for traditional banquet dinner, wedding reception, guess I won’t anymore, even I had my wedding reception banquet here 10 years ago. Guess 10 years is a very long time and thing changed.Won’t be back for sure, with that amount of money I’m paying, I didn’t get the equivalent food or service I deserve

Author: K. Patrick
Review: Le Parlour Cafe Studio is a fairly nice and calming cafe experience that promises a "book lover's experience" alongside traditional cafe cuisine. I found it to be an overall pleasant dining experience but there are some aspects that could …MoreLe Parlour Cafe Studio is a fairly nice and calming cafe experience that promises a "book lover's experience" alongside traditional cafe cuisine. I found it to be an overall pleasant dining experience but there are some aspects that could be improved if it truly wants to be a hit among book lovers.GOOD THINGS1. Cuisine and price:The cafe serves mostly western food so if you're a fan of pastas, salads, tea cakes, cheesy fries and grilled chicken, I'm sure you'll enjoy it. Quality of food is excellent although it took some time to be prepared. The prices are a bit steep but I assume it's to pay for the very nice ambiance and furniture. Bonus points for the vegan cuisine and the excellent fries.2. The staff:The staff were very friendly, welcoming and professional. I especially liked how knowledgeable the manager was about the cakes and even gave detailed recommendations about the top cakes I should try (the Hazelnut Opera was great!) Definitely keep up this type of service.3. The Music and Cafe AtmosphereLoved the jazz music and indie mixes as well as the lovely, cozy and chill cafe atmosphere. The abundance of tea lights, floral displays and aromatherapy used definitely showed great dedication to keeping a cafe atmosphere. This is the perfect spot to take your date to or for a casual teatime with friends.BAD THINGS1. The cleanliness of the toilet::( Sadly, when I went in to check the toilet, the floor was dirty because patrons trekked in their mud and dirt from their outdoor shoes. An important suggestion: Why don't you place a "no shoes" sign and provide slippers for us to wear so the floor of the toilet would remain clean? This will save a lot of money and maintain your cleanliness.2. The arrangement of the booksThis was the most disappointing. The cafe did not offer a book lover's experience at all as the books were outdated, mostly children's books and heck, they were stacked up in impossibly high places. They were also hard to access since you had to dig past rows of other books. My suggestion? I ordered chicken tomyam, butter prawn, mango salad, omelette, mango sticky rice and butterfly pea drink.1. Tomyam - moderate taste, chicken portion was very limited. I think I only found 5-6 pieces of chicken inside tomyam that costs around rm25! It was really overpriced.2. Butter prawn - this is the best dish that I had. It was tasty and the prawn size is big. Again, overpriced dish and the omelette was oily too.5. Sticky mango rice - the sticky rice was so hard and the santan was tasteless. The mango was a bit sour too. For RM12, it's not really worth it.6. Butterfly pea drink - I love this drink, it was refreshing and the price was affordable, RM4. You can try.Overall, the price was quite overrated and the taste of food was moderate for me. In additon, I hope they would provide a bigger plate for customers. Author: K. Patrick
Review: Food was a bit pricey (a meal of eggs Benedict costs up to RM 22.50, drinks are about RM 10-18+) so prepare your wallet if you come here. Ambience is beautiful, cozy and classy. Gives off a rich, cafe aesthetic. Suitable for bringing your …MoreFood was a bit pricey (a meal of eggs Benedict costs up to RM 22.50, drinks are about RM 10-18+) so prepare your wallet if you come here. Ambience is beautiful, cozy and classy. Gives off a rich, cafe aesthetic. Suitable for bringing your friends, significant others or hosting a small, intimate brunch. Very sophisticated. However, if you have 5 people you won't be allowed to pull your tables close to one another. Seating is confined to small, intimate tables that sit 2 people or 3 people at most. Nevertheless, servers were friendly and service was quite fast. Recommended to book reservations early since this place is usually full on weekends. My friends recommend the snow crab croissant, matcha drinks and jasmine green tea cake. I found the cake to taste rather floral. Suitable for people who like brunch. Disability parking provided.

Author: Alexey Zilber
Review: Looks like Kuching has another coffee heavy hitter in town.  Went here with the fam with a reserved table.  Order is at the counter, and there's only one menu, so better order right there and quick.  I'm not sure what's up, but the kitchen …MoreLooks like Kuching has another coffee heavy hitter in town.  Went here with the fam with a reserved table.  Order is at the counter, and there's only one menu, so better order right there and quick.  I'm not sure what's up, but the kitchen closed, and then opened about an hour or two later... The coffee was great. Flat white was pretty perfect. Really couldn't ask for more.The kids got some of the more exotic drinks which were great too, and I chased everything with a Shiso mint tea.  The food is also good.  Mostly sandwiches, but my wife had an eggs benedict which was quite good as well.  I tried the snow crab croissant, which, while quite pricey, was delicious, and I shamelessly inhaled it in 5 minutes. My son and his cousin ordered the brownies, twice. That says alot about the brownies. We tried most of the cakes, and some cookies.  I prefer my cookies cold, so make sure to let  them know not to warm them up.  Had a pretty good time here.  I should mention the staff were super helpful and got us to the car when it was raining. Free wifi was great and grab payments accepted. Can't think of a better way to spend the evening in Saradise.
Location: Ground Floor, Lot 20, Block A1, Saradise Kuching, Jalan Stutong, Kuching

Author: Greg K
Review: The only standard for fine dining in Kuching that matters at the moment. The chef's attention to detail, plating and food quality are of a very high standard; especially when compared to other restaurants with similar price points. Service …MoreThe only standard for fine dining in Kuching that matters at the moment. The chef's attention to detail, plating and food quality are of a very high standard; especially when compared to other restaurants with similar price points. Service is on point. Water was refilled frequently, staff is pleasant, and timing of the food was well organized. The restaurant takes customer feedback very seriously, so do not hesitate to bring any concerns to the their attention.The menu is not extensive, as should be the case for most fine dining establishments. Better that they do fewer items well than many items mediocre. Angus ribeye cooked perfectly as asked. I've tried the seabass and red snapper, but prefer the red snapper for its accompaniments and texture of the fish. Ginger cod is ok. Fresh oysters are great. Beef carpaccio excellent. Beef tartare good. Mushroom soup is tasty. I would highly recommend the apple pie looking dessert with ice cream. Molten cake with ice cream is delicious as well.If you frequent TJ, T's, and Zn, this place will blow all of them out of the water. Great for special occasions or when you want to treat yourself and others to good western cuisine as it's an intimate setting with a view. They have two musicians playing modern day classics as well which is a nice touch. Leave the children at home.
Location: 93100, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman, Kuching, Sarawak

They arrived first and were seated upstairs but nobody came to take their order, my sister in-law went downstairs to order but was chased back up. When we arrived, we took the liberty to go back down to place our order. After placing our orders we sat and waited. Only some of our orders arrived and the drinks came very late. After waiting for some time and our food didn't seem to be coming we decided to leave and when we went to pay they had the audacity to charge us for the food which weren't served. Only after insisting we didn't get the food did they latrr waived the amount. We  came to support local businesses and as the world is opening up more people are going out to eat with family and friends yet they don't seem to have enough staff to take orders and serve food.  How to help such local businesses when they don't help themselves to improve and deliver quality service? Really spoil our mood for the day. I'll think twice if I ever have to come here in the future...

Review: What makes tHe Spring unique is that it is so well thought-out from start to finish. Unusually for Sarawak, it is a tenant-only mall with no shopping lots sold to third parties. This gives tHe Spring’s management total control over the …MoreWhat makes tHe Spring unique is that it is so well thought-out from start to finish. Unusually for Sarawak, it is a tenant-only mall with no shopping lots sold to third parties. This gives tHe Spring’s management total control over the quality and value offered, a responsibility they take very seriously indeed, providing a host of value added services, including wheelchair and mobility scooters on loan for disabled shoppers and baby stroller on loan for families with small children. Best of all, car parking is plentiful (1,200 spaces) and very affordable, while bicycle parking spaces are provided free of charge.tHe Spring’s main claim to fame is the overall shopping experience. The focus is on quality products sold by official manufacturer outlets or fully authorised dealers, with world-class brands such as, Coach, Habib Jewels, Sony, Timberland, La Senza, Esprit, Pandora, Guess,Sephora, Uniqlo, Khiels & L’Occitane and MPH Bookstore, many of whom made their first appearance in Sarawak.The concourses are spacious and brightly lit, yet not crammed with promotional displays and exhibits, so the mall never feels crowded, even on the busiest days. There are frequent events and activities taking place, well planned and properly managed to enhance the shopping and dining activities.Its yearly Community Fun Run event, tHe Spring Live Active Run, is in its sixth year and continues to garner new and returning participants, both local and international. Aside from promoting health and fitness, it serves as a platform in giving back to the local charities.The mall offers over 120 retail outlets, anchored by a Parkson department store and a well-stocked supermarket carrying a wide range of imported foodstuffs and beverages. These are supplemented by dozens of food and drink outlets, including major international brands such as Starbucks, Sakae Sushi, Big Apple Donut, Secret Recipe, KFC & Pizza Hut, Sushi King, Manhattan Fish Market, and Kenny Rogers Roasters.tHe Spring’s FoodBazaar houses a variety of cuisines in its 15 stalls with best-sellers and favourites such as the champion Singapore Chicken Rice and Madam Tang’s Laksa. Its recent uplift is designed by an international award-winning designer, drawing inspiration from a garden theme that seats hundreds of people.The overall experience would not be complete without entertainment, and tHe Spring offers an 8-screen Cineplex, the first in Sarawak to feature dedicated 3-D screens, and an indoor playground, Kidz Paradise

Review: Came across this restaurant while walking towards Chong Choon Cafe for breakfast. There were many local customers having breakfast in it. So, I decided to come here for brunch the next day. I had "kolo mee" with mixed soup for RM 10.00 per …MoreCame across this restaurant while walking towards Chong Choon Cafe for breakfast. There were many local customers having breakfast in it. So, I decided to come here for brunch the next day. I had "kolo mee" with mixed soup for RM 10.00 per set. The noodles were springy and it reminded me of instant noodles. The soup was light but the taste had an obvious presence of chinese cooking wine. Although, it was not my preference but, I think it was a special feature for this stall. In a nutshell, this place is worth a try for the authentic local taste.

Author: Stephanie Cristal D.
Review: On Mother's Day, we ended up at Wonderboom with all our top 5 favorite Chinese restaurants being fully booked by noon. Looking at the super interesting and attractive varieties on the menu, I was so excited to try so many things and thanks …MoreOn Mother's Day, we ended up at Wonderboom with all our top 5 favorite Chinese restaurants being fully booked by noon. Looking at the super interesting and attractive varieties on the menu, I was so excited to try so many things and thanks to me, I brought my family into quite a terrible dinner as most of the food were overly hyped but didn't taste so delicious. Oh! The only thing I liked was the sweet potato fries. If you do come here, don't forget to order that. RM12.90We tried over 10 items on the menu excluding drinks etc. and spent over RM420. I was into spending time with my family over the meal and didn't take the pictures of the food except for the Shinjuku rice bowl, all because I was shocked to see how different that slice of unagi was from the depicted picture on the menu. It was like only a quarter of the one whole unagi slice. RM27.90Let's talk about the other things we ordered, which I got to try. The MI-SO Yummy (Japanese miso porridge with soft-shelled crab), to me, the wrongest thing they did with this dish was to marinate the fried soft-shelled crab in curry powder. It just didn't go well with the miso side of the Japanese cuisine. Other than that, the porridge itself was okay, nothing too special. RM25.90Next, the Ooh - Ma - Mi, claimed to be the sirloin steak at its best, ordered by my big-fan-of-steak husband, and he didn't touch it any more after his first bite. RM48.90Cousin to the sirloin steak was the Hey Shortie, beef short ribs that tasted like the beef stew you commonly get to eat during Raya, in bigger slice (with the rib) and tender. But definitely didn't live up to the impression its name gave us. RM38.90The Red Sea, seafood red curry with vegetable rice bowl. Hmm, what should I say about it? It was small in portion with limited seafood among the vegetables, and the taste was not like any curry that I knew, maybe a little like the Thai green curry style. RM20.90Okay, the Smells Are Free - mushroom noodle bowl in garlic butter oil. Indeed, it was just smell and didn't taste much.. But it's not free, you all. RM14.90I didn't get to taste a few other dishes, so I will share my review on just what I have tasted.Oh yea, and the desserts, expect around RM18 per slice with small portion. We ordered the Mango Cheese and the seasonal special, Tiramisu. The Tiramisu fingers were soaked in Kahlua which attracted me to try it (but overly soaked, so be careful not to get drunk, just in case).Nevertheless, the friendly staff earned the 2 stars I'm giving.

Review: I grow up eating dimsum in the peninsular Malaysia and it is one of the thing that I occasionally miss living here. Right off the bat: disappointing. I still give this place 4-stars as I don’t want to ruin the average rating. But they have …MoreI grow up eating dimsum in the peninsular Malaysia and it is one of the thing that I occasionally miss living here. Right off the bat: disappointing. I still give this place 4-stars as I don’t want to ruin the average rating. But they have to up their game.Ok where do we start. I ordered what i consider the basics of dimsum. The lo mai gai (glutinous rice with chicken) is tasteless with a strip of shitake smaller than my pinky. The chicken is not well marinated. The char siew bao is not appealing, you know that smooth shiny outer layer instead of the fluffy pillowy exterior? That. It’s flat and the fillings are dry, tasteless and the meat is lean instead of juicy fatty goodness. And it’s dry. The siew mai (sio bee) doesn’t feel like it’s worth the RM1 they charge. Plenty of places in town serves better without calling itself a dimsum place.In a town like Kuching where good dimsum is nonexistent (hello Miri you have it good) this place has all the opportunity to be a rockstar in town. I came to try because I want to be optimistic. But this place fell short. Hope they can improve. I’m not vengefully angry just plain disappointed. C’mon Hock Hai!

Location: 52, Jln Padungan, Kuching, Sarawak

Author: Iise Chew
Review: Anyone here ever tried Sarawak’s ‘Lui Cha’? 🌿🌱☘️🍀It’s the meanest, greenest concoction of herbs blended into a soup that’s deemed …MoreAnyone here ever tried Sarawak’s ‘Lui Cha’? 🌿🌱☘️🍀It’s the meanest, greenest concoction of herbs blended into a soup that’s deemed as a potion for rejuvenation for the Hakka community. Served together with Sarawak red rice, it packs a punch.Believe me, Sarawak’s version of this dish is an entire different world as compared to West Malaysia; I’ve tried Johor and KL’s version, nothing can beat the strength and bitterness of Sarawak’s Lui Cha.It is so indescribably bitter - when I first came to Kuching, in order to impress Michelle Goh Vivian’s parents, somewhat like passage of rite I dived into Lui Cha.At my first bite, I quietly exclaimed to Michelle, “Hey, I think it’s spoilt,” hoping not to catch her parent’s eyes. It was incredulously bitter. She laughed at me and said it tastes perfectly fine!With perseverance and multiple trials of this dish, I’ve now come to love it and it happens to be a must have whenever I go back to Kuching. I am also married to Michelle now hehe.This Lui Cha stall in Huo Min Cafe is a family favourite - serving perhaps the largest portion of greens for the same price as other stalls. For those who want to look younger, many of the locals here swear by this dish. 😃 — with Michelle Goh Vivian and 2 others at Huo Min Cafe (和民园).
Location: 171-178, Q4A, Taman Hui Sing, Kuching, Sarawak

Author: kok leong yuen
Review: I am a big fan of rojak. I am serious. I used to eat rojak as lunch for every weekend when I was staying in the peninsular. So trust me when I said I know my rojak (or pasembur as some might call it). I think Kueh Fah's Rojak Ayam Satok …MoreI am a big fan of rojak. I am serious. I used to eat rojak as lunch for every weekend when I was staying in the peninsular. So trust me when I said I know my rojak (or pasembur as some might call it). I think Kueh Fah's Rojak Ayam Satok makes pretty good rojak. I brought a friend along but she said it was slightly sweet for her taste. Obviously she didn't know her rojak. D'oh. The quintessential rojak sauce is made from peanut sauce not too unlike satay's (or Gado-Gado) sauce- of course it is going to be sweet! The taste could be tweaked with the provided delicious sambal kicap- on free flow.I don't know what kind of service or level of cleanliness that all these other reviewers are complaining but when in Rome, as they say... It is a kopitiam, you don't expect Ritz Carlton's level of service do you? Never had any problem with the service (visited many times), waiters are quick to wipe the table and ask for drinks order. The rojak is also served very quickly. I am writing this review in English so that more people can give it a try and crowd this place (to the detriment of my next visit!). I know some others who claim the 'other' rojak establishment (which you have to queue to take your own food) is better, but I am a big fan of this one.
Location: Kuching, Sarawak

Author: Jarod Yong
Review: My go-to for Banana Leaf Rice in Kuching. I usually share a Teh Halia Kau with my wife as it comes in a big mug. …MoreMy go-to for Banana Leaf Rice in Kuching. I usually share a Teh Halia Kau with my wife as it comes in a big mug.With the Banana Leaf Rice, I usually ask for dried chilli which is the perfect spicy & salty accompaniment to the rice dish. I really love how the individual condiments contribute different textures & flavors to the dish. Nothing like crunchy cucumber slices to cool you down after a mouthful of dried chilli, pineapple chutney, & rice soaked in curry.The best part is you can have as much as you want for the same price. The server was shocked when I asked for more rice. I tend to overeat every time I have banana leaf rice. Perhaps it's because I eat with my fingers &, trust me, it's the best way to enjoy this dish. Somehow it tastes better when you're licking it off your fingers.I think the rojak, roti, & tosai are so-so. I've yet to find a great rojak or tosai in Kuching. Mee goreng can be pretty good depending on the mood of the cook. 🤣The proprietor shared a secret with me. Never order lassi in Kuching. There isn't a source of fresh milk here so the lassi you're gulping down at any establishment would have been made from powder & lack the body & full cream goodness of fresh milk.
Location: & Rubber Road, 7G, Lorong Rubber 1, Kuching, Sarawak
